policy: Exact reviewed object identities only. Passband-specific photometry, conditional model ranges, withheld radial-velocity evidence, published rotation models and GCVS variability are display metadata; they never fill Johnson V, scalar mass, radius or the space-motion astrometry bundle.

mass_range.reference: Luhman 2014, ApJL 786 L18, abstract and Section 3.2
mass_range.scope: Evolutionary-model mass range for WISE 0855-0714, conditional on an assumed age of 1-10 Gyr. Neither a dynamical mass measurement nor a confidence interval; no midpoint mass or measured age is adopted. The 3-10 Jupiter-mass range is also supported by Rowland et al. 2024, Section IV (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.14541v2).

infrared_photometry.reference: Luhman 2014, ApJL 786 L18, Table 1 and Section 2.3
infrared_photometry.scope: Apparent W2 magnitude of the moving WISE 0855-0714 object after subtracting the two stationary background sources using their Spitzer [4.5] photometry. Preserves the published 0.05 mag uncertainty. Infrared snapshot photometry, not Johnson V and not the blended All-Sky W2=13.63 measurement.

radial_velocity_review.reference: Rowland et al. 2024, Appendix B, Figure 7
radial_velocity_review.reason: JWST/NIRSpec atmospheric retrievals fit radial velocity, but the authors attribute the discrepant results from the two datasets to wavelength-calibration differences. No calibrated bulk radial velocity is adopted from these fits. Proper-motion-derived tangential speed cannot substitute for radial velocity; space motion remains transverse only.

mass_range.scope: Evolutionary scenarios at assumed ages of 1 and 5 Gyr; neither a confidence interval nor measured age. Temperature: 502 +/- 10 K at 1 Gyr and 539 +/- 12 K at 5 Gyr; mass: 10.7 +/- 0.2 and 25.8 +/- 0.9 Jupiter masses; radius: 1.0192 +/- 0.0005 and 0.886 +/- 0.005 Jupiter radii, respectively. Endpoint uncertainties are distinct from the span between the scenarios. No midpoint scalar is adopted.

infrared_photometry.scope: Measured JWST/NIRISS F480M snapshot, not Johnson V. The Table 2 F150W=17.26 +/- 0.03 entry for UGPS-0722 is synthesized from earlier spectroscopy, not measured in this JWST exposure.

infrared_photometry.reference: Albert et al. 2025, AJ 169, 163, Tables 2 and 4
infrared_photometry.scope: Measured JWST/NIRCam F480M snapshot, not Johnson V. The same exposure gives F150W=21.316 +/- 0.014 Vega mag. Identity is confirmed by Table 4 coordinates RA=249.9258850, Dec=-68.8055121 deg at MJD 60123.90787, despite a contradictory full designation in Table 1. HST/WFC3 F127M=20.00 +/- 0.02 Vega mag on 2019-03-11 is independently reported by Fontanive et al. (2023), Tables 2-3 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09923).

rotation.reference: Monnier et al. 2012, ApJL 761, L3, Table 2 (concordance model)
rotation.scope: CHARA/MIRC gravity-darkened model: equatorial radius 2.726 +/- 0.006 and polar radius 2.418 +/- 0.012 solar radii, rotation period 0.71 +/- 0.02 d, seen nearly pole-on (inclination 6.2 +/- 0.4 deg). The period fit uses a 0.71 d magnetic-field prior. Equatorial velocity is derived as 2 pi R_eq / P; the paper estimates about 195 km/s.

rotation.reference: Che et al. 2011, ApJ 732, 68, Table 3 (beta-free model)
rotation.scope: CHARA/MIRC gravity-darkened model: equatorial radius 3.79 (+0.10/-0.09) and polar radius 3.06 (+0.08/-0.07) solar radii, 1.12 (+0.03/-0.04) rotations per day, inclination 19.9 deg. The period is the inverse rotation rate; equatorial velocity is derived as 2 pi R_eq / P.

rotation.reference: Zhao et al. 2009, ApJ 701, 209, Table 4 (standard beta = 0.25 model)
rotation.scope: CHARA/MIRC gravity-darkened model of Rasalhague A: equatorial radius 2.871 +/- 0.020 and polar radius 2.390 +/- 0.014 solar radii, inclination 87.70 +/- 0.43 deg, model v sin i 237 km/s. The authors prefer this fixed-beta model because beta and inclination are degenerate. Equatorial velocity is derived as v sin i / sin i and the period as 2 pi R_eq / v_eq.
